metadata.description: Phishing detection training dataset. Each example includes the domain/URL, label, confidence, and a structured explanation of the signals that determine the classification. Use this for few-shot prompting, fine-tuning, or as ground truth for an ML classifier.

labels.phishing: Malicious domain attempting to deceive users
labels.legitimate: Genuine domain belonging to the claimed organization

signal_taxonomy.brand_in_subdomain: A real brand name appears left of a suspicious root domain (e.g., paypal.attacker.com)
signal_taxonomy.brand_in_path: Brand name stuffed into the URL path rather than the root domain
signal_taxonomy.lookalike_tld: Uses an unusual TLD where the real brand uses .com/.org/.gov
signal_taxonomy.typosquat: Domain is a minor misspelling or character substitution of a real brand
signal_taxonomy.homograph: Uses Unicode/IDN characters that visually resemble ASCII characters
signal_taxonomy.excessive_hyphens: Multiple hyphens used to mimic brand-keyword combinations
signal_taxonomy.excessive_subdomains: Unusually deep subdomain nesting to bury the real root domain
signal_taxonomy.keyword_stuffing: Multiple trust-building keywords in domain (secure, login, verify, update)
signal_taxonomy.legitimate_tld_match: Domain uses the expected TLD for its category (bank→.com, gov→.gov)
signal_taxonomy.brand_is_root: The brand name IS the root domain, not buried in a subdomain
signal_taxonomy.aged_consistent_domain: Domain pattern consistent with long-running legitimate service
signal_taxonomy.url_shortener: Uses a URL shortener to hide real destination
signal_taxonomy.ip_address_url: Uses raw IP address instead of a domain name
signal_taxonomy.free_hosting: Hosted on a free hosting/website builder platform
signal_taxonomy.mismatched_context: Domain name doesn't match the claimed sender context
signal_taxonomy.punycode: Uses punycode encoding (xn--) to create visual lookalikes

examples.label: legitimate
examples.explanation: PayPal's actual root domain. The brand name is the root, uses .com, no suspicious patterns.

examples.label: phishing
examples.explanation: PayPal's real domain is paypal.com. Adding 'secure-login' via hyphens is a classic phishing pattern — the brand is used but the root domain is entirely attacker-controlled.

examples.label: legitimate
examples.explanation: Root domain is paypal.com. 'secure' is just a subdomain on PayPal's own domain — this is a normal pattern for large companies.

examples.label: phishing
examples.explanation: Root domain is secure-verify.com (attacker-controlled). PayPal is only a subdomain — the attacker owns everything after the last dot before the TLD.

examples.label: phishing

examples.label: phishing
